title: Relative Picard detection by the three identity faces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For $i=1,2,3$, let $p_i:G_i\to S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with identity $e_i$ and geometrically connected fibres. Group scheme means that addition, inverse and identity are morphisms over $S$ satisfying the commutative group identities; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume either that every $p_i$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], or that $S$ is normal and every geometric fibre of every $G_i$ is semiabelian. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Semiabelian means that over an algebraically closed residue-field extension $k$ the fibre is an extension, exact as fppf sheaves, $1\to(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r\to G_{i,k}\to A\to1$, where $r\geq0$, $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$, and $A$ is a proper smooth geometrically connected commutative $k$-group scheme. Put $P=G_1\times_SG_2\times_SG_3$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and let $j_i$ be the morphism from the product of the other two factors to $P$ inserting $e_i$ in coordinate $i$. If $M$ is any invertible $\mathcal O_P$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] such that $j_i^*M\simeq\mathcal O_{\prod_{h\ne i}G_h}$ for each $i$, then $M\simeq\mathcal O_P$. Pullbacks are tensor inverse images [def-pc-module-pullback]. No trivialization of $M$, cubical structure or symmetry condition is supplied as part of this assertion.

proof.text: We use the following geometry throughout, also after restricting the base to an open or extending a residue field. Smoothness, flatness and local finite presentation are stable under base change and composition by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]; finite presentation and separatedness are preserved by products using [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality, lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. Thus every finite product of the $G_i$ is smooth, separated and finitely presented. In case (a) its structure map is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] and proper base change in the locality node. Its fibres are geometrically connected: a product projection is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], flatness and local finite presentation above, and surjective by its identity section, with connected fibres, so a clopen partition of its source descends to a clopen partition of its connected target (the two images are disjoint open sets); iterate after every field extension. Each nonempty smooth geometrically connected scheme over a field is geometrically integral: apply [lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry-core] over that field, and again over every extension field. The identity sections ensure nonemptiness. In particular all products used below have geometrically integral fibres.

source.place: Tag 0BF4, first paragraph of proof: geometry and universal structure sheaf pushforward; geometry core Tags 034F, 056T, 01UA

proof.text: Here is the unit test needed for uniqueness. Write $H=G_1\times_SG_2\times_SG_3$. If a unit $u$ on $P=H$ restricts to $1$ on each single-coordinate axis, pull it back to $H^3$ by $r(h_1,h_2,h_3)=((h_1)_1,(h_2)_2,(h_3)_3)$. Its restriction to each $H$-axis is $1$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-group-unit-axis-factorization] with group $H$ and $n=3$. Step 1 checks its smoothness, finite-presentation, connected-fibre and proper hypotheses in (a); in (b), normality implies reducedness since an integrally closed domain has no nonzero nilpotents. Thus $r^*u=1$. Pull back by $a(g_1,g_2,g_3)=((g_1,e_2,e_3),(e_1,g_2,e_3),(e_1,e_2,g_3))$, for which $ra=\mathrm{id}_P$, to obtain $u=1$. This test applies over open subschemes and over fields. In particular two generating sections of the same line that agree on all three faces are equal: their quotient is a global unit, and each axis is contained in a face.

source.place: Proposition 12.48, identity (79); reduction from different factors to the already stated repeated-factor unit lemma

proof.text: Fix, once on $S$, generating sections $b_i$ of $M|_{F_i}$ supplied by the three triviality assumptions, with $F_i=j_i(\prod_{h\ne i}G_h)$ interpreted through its parameter scheme. The section $r_0=b_1|_{(e_1,e_2,e_3)}$ generates the identity pullback. Choose a generating section $c_k$ of $M$ on each axis by restricting any $b_i$ with $i\ne k$, then multiplying by the pullback of its identity-value ratio so that $c_k(e)=r_0$. For $\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}$ define units $a_{ij}=c_j/(b_i|_{\text{axis }j})$, $a_{ik}=c_k/(b_i|_{\text{axis }k})$ and $d_i=r_0/b_i(e)$ on the indicated axes or on $S$. Both $a_{ij}$ and $a_{ik}$ have identity value $d_i$. Replace $b_i$ by $b_i'=b_i\,\pi_j^*a_{ij}\,\pi_k^*a_{ik}/p^*d_i$ on $F_i$. Restriction to axis $j$ cancels $a_{ik}(e)=d_i$, giving $c_j$; similarly for $k$. The new face sections therefore agree on every pairwise intersection (an axis) and on the triple intersection. These operations are pullback, tensor multiplication and division in local rank-one bases, so commute with every base change.

source.place: I 2.6 geometric cube input; agent elementary normalization of the unchosen face trivializations

proof.text:
Whenever $M$ has a generating section $t$ over $P_U$, it can be made to equal all three $b_i'$ there. Let $z_i:P_U\to P_U$ replace coordinate $i$ by its identity, and for a nonempty subset $I$ write $z_I=\prod_{i\in I}z_i$. Put $f_I=(b_i'/t)|_{F_I}$ with $F_I$ the face where every coordinate in $I$ is the identity, choosing any $i\in I$; step 3 makes this independent of $i$. Pull these units to $P_U$ using $z_I$. Define
$$v=\frac{\prod_{|I|=1}z_I^*f_I}{\prod_{|I|=2}z_I^*f_I}\,z_{\{1,2,3\}}^*f_{\{1,2,3\}}.$$
On $F_j$, the factors indexed by $I$ and $I\cup\{j\}$ cancel whenever $j\notin I$, leaving precisely $f_{\{j\}}$. Hence $tv$ is a generating section with the prescribed face restrictions. Here $z_I^*$ on $f_I$ means pullback from the parameter scheme $F_I$. This gives existence of normalized sections from triviality, using no cubical structure on $M$.

source.place: I 2.6; agent inclusion-exclusion formula for compatible face frames

proof.text: First suppose (a). Regard $P$ as $(G_1\times_SG_3)\times_{G_3}(G_2\times_SG_3)$ and write $q:P\to G_3$. Step 1 and [lem-sc-proper-flat-global-sections] give universal structure-sheaf pushforward for $G_1$, $G_2$, their product and all their base changes. Apply [lem-sc-picard-diagonal-locally-closed] to $q,M$ to get an immersion $C\hookrightarrow G_3$ representing the locus where $M$ is pulled back from the parameter. Its finite locally free base module necessarily has rank one, by restriction along the section $(e_1,e_2,\mathrm{id})$. The geometrically integral fibres in step 1 let [lem-sc-picard-locus-closed] make $C$ closed. At a point $c\in C$, $M_c$ is trivial, since a line over a field is free. The two identity slices $F_1,F_2$ are trivial by hypothesis. Thus [lem-sc-picard-product-open], applied over $G_3$, gives an open neighbourhood $U$ of $c$ with $M|_{P_U}$ trivial. Its universal property makes $U\to G_3$ factor through $C$ scheme-theoretically. Consequently $C$ is also open, with its open subscheme structure, not merely open as a set.

source.place: Tags 0BDP, 0BF0, 0BF3; proof of Tag 0BF4, closed and open triviality locus

proof.text: The third face says $M|_{G_1\times_SG_2\times_Se_3(S)}$ is trivial, so the universal property gives a factorization $e_3:S\to C$. For each $s\in S$, the clopen subset $C\cap(G_3)_s$ of the connected fibre contains $e_3(s)$ and is therefore the whole fibre. Thus the open subscheme $C$ of step 5 has all points of $G_3$, hence equals $G_3$. Its representing property now gives $M\simeq q^*N$ for a line $N$ on $G_3$. Pull back along $(e_1,e_2,\mathrm{id})$: the left side is trivial since this map factors through $F_1$, and the right side is $N$. Thus $N$ and $M$ are trivial. This proves (a), with no connectedness assumption on $S$ and no reducedness assumption on $S$.

source.place: Tag 0BF4 proof, final trivialization; replace global connectedness of Z by a section meeting every connected fibre

proof.text: For (b), first work over an arbitrary field $k$ with three groups satisfying the geometric semiabelian hypothesis, and a line $M$ trivial on their identity faces. Apply [lem-sfb-geometric-semiabelian-split-quotient] successively to the three groups, enlarging the field each time. After these three finite Galois extensions, take the normal closure of the composite over $k$; finite separability ensures it is again a finite Galois extension $K/k$. We have split-torus torsors $q_i:(G_i)_K\to A_i$ with $A_i$ abelian varieties. Their product $q:P_K\to A_1\times_KA_2\times_KA_3=:A$ is a torsor under the product split torus: flatness, surjectivity and finite presentation follow from base change and composition, and the torsor isomorphism is the product of the displayed kernel-action isomorphisms. By step 1 the target $A$ is a smooth separated finite-type $K$-scheme. Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-line-pullback] to obtain an invertible module $N$ on $A$ and an isomorphism $q^*N\simeq M_K$.

source.place: Theorem 3.1; split-torus line pullback prerequisite, followed by the field cube argument

proof.text:
For $I\subseteq\{1,2,3\}$ let $z_I:A\to A$ set the coordinates in $I$ equal to the corresponding identity; $z_\varnothing=\mathrm{id}$. Define
$$C(N)=\bigotimes_{I\subseteq\{1,2,3\}}(z_I^*N)^{(-1)^{|I|}},$$
where exponent $-1$ denotes the dual line. On the $j$-th identity face the factors for $I$ not containing $j$ pair with those for $I\cup\{j\}$: the two maps agree there, and the exponents are opposite. Evaluation of a line with its dual gives a trivial line, so all three face restrictions of $C(N)$ are trivial. Each $q_i$ preserves the identity, hence $qz_I=z_Iq$. The tensor-pullback formula gives $q^*C(N)\simeq C(q^*N)\simeq C(M_K)$. For each nonempty $I$, $z_I$ on $P_K$ factors through an identity face, making $z_I^*M_K$ trivial. Therefore $C(M_K)\simeq M_K$ as invertible modules. The trivializations used in this cancellation need no compatibility.

source.place: I Theorem 5.1; agent face-cancellation operator on the pulled-back quotient line

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-general-theorem-of-cube] over $K$ to $X=A_1$, $Y=A_2$, $Z=A_3$, the identity points and the line $C(N)$. The first two varieties are proper and geometrically integral by step 1, the third is connected, and its identity is a $K$-point at which the third face of $C(N)$ is trivial by step 8. It follows that $C(N)$ is trivial. Pulling back gives $M_K\simeq\mathcal O_{P_K}$. Notice that the cube theorem has been applied to the proper abelian quotient; no properness of $(G_i)_K$ has been asserted.

source.place: Tag 0BF4 over a field; Milne I Theorem 5.1

proof.text: The normalized face sections $b_i'$ of step 3 are defined over $k$. Normalize a generating section of $M_K$ by step 4, obtaining $t_K$ restricting to their base changes. For every $\gamma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)$, the canonical descent comparison identifies $\gamma^*M_K$ with $M_K$, and $\gamma^*t_K$ and $t_K$ have identical face restrictions. Step 2, over $K$, implies they are equal. The algebra isomorphism in [lem-exc-finite-galois-tensor-decomposition](1), $K\otimes_kK\cong\prod_\gamma K$, identifies the two pullbacks of $t_K$ on the overlap with exactly these equal sections. Thus the generating section and its inverse map agree on the fpqc overlap. Apply [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] to the finite faithfully flat field cover of $P$: its full faithfulness descends the section and its inverse, giving $M\simeq\mathcal O_P$ over $k$. This proves the field assertion over the original residue field, including imperfect fields.

source.place: Tag 023T, full faithfulness and descent of compatible trivializations; finite Galois tensor decomposition

proof.text: Return to (b) over the given normal $S$. For every $s\in S$, the residue-field groups $(G_i)_s$ are smooth separated geometrically connected and geometrically semiabelian. The face trivializations pull back to their identity faces. Steps 7--10, applied over $\kappa(s)$, prove $M_s$ trivial over that field, not just after algebraic closure. The smooth separated finitely presented morphism $P\to S$ has nonempty geometrically connected fibres by step 1. Hence [lem-sfb-normal-base-fibrewise-line-locality] gives an open cover $\{U_a\}$ of $S$ and lines $N_a$ with $M|_{P_{U_a}}\simeq p^*N_a$. Pullback along the all-identity section makes $N_a$ isomorphic to $M$ at the identity, which is trivial by any face. Thus $M|_{P_{U_a}}$ is trivial. This is the only passage from field fibres to a possibly non-Noetherian normal base, and it is supplied by the cited locality statement.

source.place: Tag 0BD7 and its explicitly stated arbitrary-normal-base locality prerequisite

proof.text: For each $a$, use step 4 to choose a generating section $t_a$ of $M|_{P_{U_a}}$ restricting to the fixed $b_i'$. On $P_{U_a\cap U_b}$ their quotient is a unit equal to $1$ on all faces, hence on all axes. The unit test of step 2 gives $t_a=t_b$. The sheaf axiom glues these sections to a global section $t$; their local inverse maps glue as well, so $t$ generates $M$ globally. This proves (b). If $S$ is empty the sheaf is uniquely trivial; if one group is the trivial group, the corresponding face already equals the product, so the same argument includes that case. No face trivialization, symmetry or cubical structure is added to the conclusion or hypotheses: choices made in step 3 are only proof data.
